reviews.review:
The game is very very fun, butttttttttttttt (literally) the game has one fatal flaw and that is a heavy stuttering problem you get seemingly random while playing where the game will just constantly freeze or stutter for 1-5 seconds or just straight up crash, this is especially problematic because like for Sigma Sector for instance, the game has to reload everything before the mission every time as opposed to the more open world areas where the game eventually stops stuttering because it has fully loaded all the shaders/textures. (Mind you these missions are incredibly short, like 1-3 minutes average.

Also also this happens on any level of graphic you set the game to, which doesn't necessarily mean it's due to not enough memory or ram, but if you are close to the ceiling of memory (%80+) than the amount of times the stutters will occur will be much more common, so it's definitely possible it's just a combination of Unreal Engine 5, lack of optimization (which could take time, mind you Marvel Rivals had this exact issue and they just fixed it within this half year). So in short, more memory will definitely not hurt and likely will improve some of the stuttering but it won't likely resolve all of it completely, it will help render everything in faster, also the game always maxes out disk space for me. So ideally you have a slightly better than mid-range PC build for this game, a solid CPU, solid GPU, and 32gb of memory (ram). Also using multiple monitors is definitely a hinderance, I use two 1440p monitors and 1440p takes significantly more resources to run than 1080's which was very noticeable until I upgraded the CPU and GPU (still is to an extent).
My gpu for reference is Nvidia GeForce - RTX 3060 (20gb of memory)
CPU - AMD Ryzen 5 - 5600 - 6 - Core Processor 
Ram - Only 16 gb of RAM/Memory (2 sticks)

Even when the game is set to very high performance in Microsoft settings, still happens, which is a shame, because this is unironically an incredibly entertaining game when it works properly, so long as you set aside the ultra aggressive brutal monetization with ironically incredibly bizarre PG verbal censorship, it's a good game all and all, story isn't half bad either. Now whether this game is worth the expensive PC build and you willing to shell out a hefty sum of money to have fun with cosmetics is entirely up to you and your situation and would actually explain some of this games lack of a large player-base. I would also ignore a lot of the criticism's in the steam reviews or about the game in general, a lot of it seems driven by ignorance or the need to be validated for their feelings. 

I will say though the game is quite complex, and by that I mean their is a LOT to learn, however the game has an amazing way of figuring it out, they actually optimized the learning process incredibly well, which is far preferred over optimizing performance over substance in my opinion (more long term player loyalty and gets new players to stick easier). 

You do have to pay attention in the story, or at least I would recommend it or you will be incredibly lost and confused (it's actually not a bad story tbh, a little silly given the cosmetic choices of characters but surprisingly good plot-line, better than most modern movies), they have tried to help with this by adding the guided Ultimate Bunny Path thing, but in my experience, it seems to pair best with the knowledge of the story as that's how you unlock the different playable missions and technically game-modes.

The worst part like most online multi-player games is the community, sometimes their incredibly sweet and helpful and you have some really good moments, but a-lot of the time they can be, annoying, insufferable, weird, meta driven/elitist, rude and unnecessarily judgmental, granted a lot of these players are in World chat, but certainly not exclusive to world chat.
Which makes it difficult to find pleasant communities centered around this game, you combine that earlier statement with the games relatively modest player count and it can be quite difficult to find consistent or at the very least not completely random in game driven match-making to play missions and you know have fun with other players, as if you do try to rely solely on the games in-game driven match-making, well it's going to be a follow the leader simulator, you desperately try to keep up with the guy one-shotting everything, and than the mission instantly finishes, it's okay for grinding stuff fast, but defeats the purpose of the "game" part.

Please keep in mind, this is a very new game, was created literally in 2024, about 2 -2 1/2 years ago from this review post (9/21/2026), so it's still going to have some flaws and it might still be trying to find it's eternal footing, but it has MASSIVE potential to be an amazing long-term favorite for many alike.
